hindiTranslation: इन्द्रियोंके विषयोंमें वैराग्यका होना, अहंकारका भी न होना और जन्म, मृत्यु, वृद्धावस्था तथा व्याधियोंमें दुःखरूप दोषोंको बारबार देखना ॥
englishTranslation: Dispassion toward sense objects, absence of ego, and constant seeing of the fault in birth, death, old age, and disease.
essence: Freedom begins when desire stops dressing suffering as reward.
speaker: Krishna
simpleMeaning: Let go of craving for sensory pleasures, drop ego, and keep seeing how birth, death, old age, and illness bring suffering.
simpleInsight: Clinging loosens when you stop romanticizing what inevitably breaks.
detailedMeaning: Krishna continues listing the qualities that reveal true understanding. Here, he points to dispassion, humility, and clear sight of life's unavoidable suffering.
modernRelevance: Visiting a grandfather in a care home, you see what age does to a strong body. Krishna counts that clear look at birth, death, old age and illness as part of knowledge, along with less ego and craving.
translationLiteral: इन्द्रियार्थेषु (in sense objects) / वैराग्यम् (dispassion) / अहङ्कारः (ego) / एव (indeed) / च (and) / जन्म (birth) / मृत्यु (death) / जरा (old age) / व्याधि (disease) / दुःख (suffering) / दोषानुदर्शनम् (seeing the fault repeatedly)
insight: Krishna asks for dispassion toward sense objects, no ego, and a steady look at birth, death, old age, disease.
